issues.body: `_live_nodes` stops at functions and lambdas, but not at `ast.GeneratorExp`. A production loop can therefore contain only `(park_starved_partition_holder(repo, target, starved) for _ in (0,))` as an expression statement. Creating that generator does not execute its element expression, yet `_live_nodes(loop)` descends into the generator and `_park_call_site` finds the call and returns `dispatch`. Thus every target can remain unparked while the new checker and shipped-tree assertion stay green. The reachability self-test has no generator-expression refusal, so it does not pin this deferred scope.
issues.fix_hint: Treat generator-expression bodies as deferred execution (while accounting for the iterable expressions that are evaluated at generator creation), and add a synthetic refusal proving a park call placed only in an unconsumed generator expression is rejected. Include the old-checker acceptance leg so the test demonstrates the intended reachability gap rather than malformed source.
issues.title: Generator expressions let an unexecuted park call pass the seam

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The reachability hardening remains bypassable by a Python deferred-execution scope that the new traversal treats as live. The otherwise useful branch and nested-function tests do not exercise this case, so the claimed structural proof is incomplete.
